discharge_recommendations.summary: Provide patient discharge information in both written and verbal formats prior to discharge. Use teach-back technique and/or motivational interviewing, give information in chunks, and check understanding.
discharge_recommendations.notes: Also recommend assessment of mental well-being with a validated tool and onward psychological referral when appropriate (IIa, B).

content.title: 15. Key messages
content.epidemiology_of_ACS: Acute coronary syndromes (ACS) include a spectrum of conditions with recent change in clinical symptoms or signs, with or without ECG changes and with or without elevations in cardiac troponin. ACS are commonly classified by ECG and presence/absence of troponin elevation into UA, NSTEMI, or STEMI. Incidence of STEMI is decreasing while NSTEMI is increasing. Sex differences exist but management strategies are generally similar for men and women.
content.diagnostic_tools_(ECG,_troponin,_and_non: Chest pain/discomfort is the most common presenting symptom. Use high-sensitivity troponin measurements and rapid rule-in/rule-out algorithms for suspected NSTE-ACS. Myocardial infarction is not the only cause of cardiomyocyte injury and troponin elevation; consider other causes in the differential. Non-invasive imaging can improve diagnostic accuracy and risk assessment.
content.STEMI_management_networks: Coordination between EMS and hospitals with common written protocols is central. EMS should transfer patients immediately to 24/7 high-volume PCI centres regardless of initial treatment strategy (PPCI or pre-hospital fibrinolysis). EMS should always alert receiving centres.
